meta.notes: Torah #43 has only 1 bechina edge in the dataset (Edge 773: בלעם ↔ דעת דקלפה). This produces a single 2-node raw component. The source text is rich with bechina language across three conceptual domains — the da'at cluster, the Moshe/holy mirror, and the speech/peh cluster — none of which are yet in the dataset for this Torah. The packages below are built from (a) the existing dataset edge and (b) gap concepts identified from explicit bechina language in the source text (see torah_43_additions.json). Every bechina node is assigned to exactly one package. No eitza relationships are used for grouping.

packages.label: דַּעַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה וּמֹשֶׁה
packages.reason: The central good cluster of Torah #43 is da'at of holiness, embodied by Moshe Rabbeinu. The Rebbe states explicitly: 'מֹשֶׁה הוּא דַּעַת' (Moshe IS da'at), and that his generation was therefore called 'דּוֹר דֵּעָה' (Generation of Knowledge). Da'at of holiness is the source of holy unions (zivug dikdushah) and of complete, unperturbed consciousness — 'when da'at is whole, there is no anger'. The polar mirror to Bilam/da'at-of-klipah is Moshe/da'at-of-holiness; the Sifri makes this comparison explicit ('lO kam keMoshe' — in Israel there arose none like Moshe, but among the nations arose Bilam). Da'at dikdushah also generates holy union (hitkashot litzaddikim vela-Torah vela-Shem Yitbarakh), which is the positive zivug — so the concept of zivug dikdushah belongs here as a bechina-expression of what holy da'at produces/is. The 'Dor De'ah' generation label is a bechina-alias for the collective human expression of Moshe's da'at.

merge_notes.reason: זיווג דקדשה is a 1-node gap concept (not yet in dataset). The source text (line 2) defines it as: הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת לְצַדִּיקִים וְאֶל הַתּוֹרָה וְאֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, drawn from דַּעַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה. Its essential nature IS holy da'at — it is what holy da'at IS (not what it causes). Merging into Package 1 because its shared nature with דעת דקדשה is the holiness-domain orientation of both concepts.

The Rebbe says: 'מֹשֶׁה הוּא דַּעַת' — Moshe IS da'at. This is a direct 'הוּא' equivalence, the strongest bechina form. Moshe is the human embodiment and personification of da'at dikdushah. He belongs in this package as the archetype/face of the concept.

packages.label: דַּעַת דִּקְלִפָּה וּבִלְעָם
packages.label_en: Da'at of the Klipah and Bilam
packages.reason: This is the evil mirror of Package 1. Bilam is explicitly called a bechina of da'at diklifah (Edge 773 in the dataset — the only pre-existing bechina edge for Torah #43). The Rebbe argues from Sifri/Zohar that just as Moshe IS holy da'at among Israel, Bilam IS klipah-da'at among the nations — this is the structural 'zeh l'umat zeh' (Kohelet 7:14: one opposite the other God made). Da'at diklifah is further defined in line 8 as מוֹתָרוֹת שֶׁל דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן — the residue/excesses of supernal da'at. Bilam's power was specifically 'kocho ba-peh' (his power was in his mouth), which is the hitgalut of his klipah-da'at. Zivug shel aveirah (sinful union) is drawn from da'at diklifah and is the evil mirror of zivug dikdushah; it belongs here as a bechina-expression of what klipah-da'at IS. The air/niuf (immorality) generated by Bilam's speech is the manifest form of klipah-da'at's harvest.

merge_notes.reason: זיווגִים שֶׁל עֲבֵרָה is a gap concept (not yet in dataset for Torah 43). Line 2 states: 'וְזִוּוּגִים שֶׁל עֲבֵרָה, נִמְשָׁכִים מִדַּעַת דִּקְלִפָּה'. Like the way זיווג דקדשה shares its nature with דעת דקדשה (good, Package 1), so too זיווגים של עברה shares its nature with דעת דקלפה — it IS the expression and embodiment of klipah-da'at in the domain of human relationships. Merged into Package 2 because its shared essential nature is klipah/evil da'at.

Line 8 defines דעת דקלפה as 'מוֹתָרוֹת שֶׁל דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן' — the excesses/overflow of supernal da'at. This is a bechina-definition of da'at diklifah (using 'שֶׁהוּא' equivalence). It is not a third entity but rather the theological explanation of what da'at diklifah IS: the residue that falls from the supernal da'at. It belongs in Package 2 as a descriptive bechina-alias of the dominant node.

packages.label: דִּבּוּר וּפֶה — הִתְגַּלּוּת הַדַּעַת
packages.label_en: Speech and Mouth — Revelation of Da'at
packages.reason: The Rebbe introduces a structural axiom that cuts across both good and evil: the mouth/speech IS the revelation of da'at — whether holy or klipah. Line 3: 'הַדִּבּוּר הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַדַּעַת'. Line 5: 'הַפֶּה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַדַּעַת'. These are explicit 'הוּא' bechina declarations establishing that dibur/peh = hitgalut da'at. The proof text used is Tehillim 19:3: 'וְלַיְלָה לְלַיְלָה יְחַוֶּה דַּעַת' — 'יְחַוֶּה is language of speech, for speech speaks what is in the da'at'. This package is NEUTRAL because the mouth/speech serves as the instrument of both domains: 'כֹּחוֹ בַּפֶּה' applies to Moshe (holy Torah speech) and to Bilam (toxic klipah speech) alike. The structural function — that speech is how da'at becomes manifest in the world — is domain-neutral. The peh is the gateway/interface that exists in both holy and klipah realms, carrying either life or poison depending on whose da'at it reveals.

merge_notes.reason: Lines 3 and 5 each contain the same bechina declaration from two angles: 'הַדִּבּוּר הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַדַּעַת' and 'הַפֶּה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַדַּעַת'. Peh (mouth), dibur (speech), and hitgalut ha-da'at (revelation of da'at) are three names for the same reality — the interface between inner da'at and its outward expression. All three form one bechina-cluster. The 'yechaaveh' verb from Tehillim 19:3 is explicitly glossed as 'lashon dibur', confirming dibur's identity as da'at-revelation.

stats.note_on_dataset_sparsity: Torah #43 is severely under-represented in the dataset with only 1 bechina edge (Edge 773: בלעם↔דעת דקלפה). The source text contains at least 6 additional explicit bechina statements. The packages above integrate both the existing edge and the gap concepts identified in torah_43_additions.json. The gap additions are proposals to expand the dataset.
stats.note_on_polarity_structure: The teaching's architecture is a classic Good/Evil mirror (framework §4): Moshe/da'at-dikdushah (Package 1, good) mirrors Bilam/da'at-diklifah (Package 2, evil), with the peh/dibur serving as the structural neutral interface (Package 3) that can carry either. The 'zeh l'umat zeh' verse (Kohelet 7:14) is explicitly cited by the Rebbe to declare this mirror structure.
